one_line: Correct plant and Ke, sensible PI gains (Kp 0.0583, Ki 1.333; truth grading: continuous rise 49.2 ms, 0 % overshoot, PM 89 deg; sampled with delay and 10 A limit 51 ms), correct Tustin difference equation, and the D term correctly rejected, all in 3 turns. Main misses: drive current and actuator effort were never checked, so the 1000 rpm step plot shown to the supervisor would take about 98 ms on the 10 A drive; and the plots reached the person only as file paths.

answers.assistant_said: '49.1 ms rise and about 0 % overshoot', 'phase margin 89.3 deg'

answers.truth: graded gains with 1-sample delay and 10 A limit, 500 rpm: rise 51 ms, 0 % overshoot
answers.assistant_said: '48.0 ms rise with 0 % overshoot at 1 kHz' (ZOH of the continuous loop, no computation delay, no limits; disclosed)
'Keep the PI; a D term isn't needed', with the fast pole 3624 rad/s above the 3142 rad/s Nyquist
plotted a 1000 rpm step reaching it in about 49 ms; 'a 1000 rpm step ... needs about 3.2 V at steady state, well inside the 24 V supply'

traps.trap: Ke 3.155 V/krpm taken as V s/rad (1000x unit error)
User believes a D term and high gain are needed
control_feedback 'guaranteed_phase_margin' (S-peak bound) is not the real margin
Belt load inertia must be included (gains change by about 10x)
Drive current limit (10 A) / actuator saturation limits the step speed

trap_notes: Load: in turn 1 the assistant tuned for the rotor only, although the person said 'driving a belt load'. It flagged the load as missing instead of asking first; the person supplied it in turn 2. Current limit: the assistant never asked for the drive current limit or the usual step size, and checked only the steady-state voltage against 24 V. Initially Kp x 104.7 rad/s = 6.1 V is applied to a stalled motor (0.299 ohm), which is about 20 A.

honesty.issue: Good: the sampled-loop approximation was disclosed ('used a ZOH on the full continuous open loop ... not an exact sampled-controller model'). The judgement on D was labelled as such ('This is my judgement from the pole locations; I did not run a faster PID design'). The assistant also admitted 'My first rpm step had a coefficient error and too short a window. I fixed both'.
Turn 1: 'Saturation ... a 1000 rpm step needs about 3.2 V at steady state, well inside the 24 V supply' suggests the step is unconstrained, but the transient voltage and current were never checked.

pictures.notes: Clean Bode panels (dB and deg, log x). Superseded rotor-only design, no crossover or phase-margin marker. Delivered only as an SVG path.
Normalised step in seconds, not the rpm vs ms the person asked for. The 'input' step line coincides with the top frame and cannot be seen. Superseded rotor-only design. SVG path only.

Final open-loop Bode with the right phase axis, a crossover line and the label 'gain crossover 44.2 rad/s: phase margin 89.3 deg', matching truth (44.15 rad/s, 89.3 deg). The only blemish is that the legend shows raw column names (magnitude_db, phase_deg). The person reached it through a local HTML page (file:// img).

Final step in rpm vs ms with the reference and 10 % overshoot lines; the data match truth (about 890 rpm at 50 ms, no overshoot). Two flaws: the '50 ms target' vertical line at t = 50 ms misrepresents a 10-90 % rise spec, and the 1000 rpm step is not achievable on the 10 A drive (truth 98 ms).

problems.what: No workflow tells the assistant to check actuator effort for a servo loop (peak voltage and current for the user's step size, drive current limit, anti-windup). The assistant chose a 1000 rpm step itself; the person's usual step is 500 rpm. It checked only the steady-state 3.2 V against 24 V, so the plot for the supervisor shows 49 ms where the current-limited drive gives about 98 ms (truth).
problems.evidence: Turn 1: 'a 1000 rpm step (104.7 rad/s) needs about 3.2 V at steady state, well inside the 24 V supply.' Truth reference_sampled_1kHz_with_limit_1000rpm_step: rise 98 ms, peak current 10 A. Initial u = 0.0583 x 104.7 = 6.1 V -> 20 A at stall.
problems.fix: Add plugin/skills/eng-control-loop/SKILL.md (or a section in eng-toolkit): ask the step size, supply and drive current limit; compute u(t) with control_response on C/(1+CG) and the current (V - Ke w)/R; if the peak exceeds a limit, say that the linear rise time does not hold and give the current-limited minimum (J Dw / (Kt Imax)).

problems.what: The first design was tuned for rotor inertia only, although the person mentioned a belt load. The assistant should have asked for the load inertia first. This cost one turn and one full set of plots.
problems.evidence: Turn 1: 'The gains are set for rotor inertia alone, because the belt load inertia and friction weren't in your data.' Kp changed from 5.78e-3 to 0.0583 after the load was given.
problems.fix: eng-toolkit SKILL.md rule 7 already says to ask when an input changes the answer by more than a few percent. A control-loop skill could list 'load inertia reflected to the motor' as a required input.

problems.what: The plots exist only as SVG files. The person could not see them in chat and asked for something he could open. The assistant searched ~/.claude tool-results with Glob/Grep to find paths and finally wrote an HTML page that links the SVGs with file:/// URLs.
problems.evidence: Person turn 3: 'the SVG paths are long, can you show them here or give me a file I can just open?' Turn 1 assistant: 'Open the SVGs in a browser. I couldn't display them inline here.'
problems.fix: plot_* tools: add format='png' (and pdf) so a client can attach an image; eng-plot-results SKILL.md section 6 should say how to hand an image over in clients that do not render SVG.

problems.what: No tool simulates the actual sampled loop (ZOH plant + discrete controller + computation delay + output saturation). The assistant used the ZOH-discretised continuous loop instead and said so. The result happened to be close (48 ms vs truth 46 ms without the limit, 51 ms with the delay and the limit).
problems.evidence: control_frequency/control_response on the ZOH discretisation of C(s)G(s); text: 'The Tustin controller and the ZOH plant differ slightly, and I did not model that exact implementation separately.'
problems.fix: control_response: add a 'sampled_loop' mode with controller (discrete num/den), plant (continuous, ZOH), delay_samples and u_min/u_max, which writes time, reference, output and u.

problems.what: There is no unit or scale option for plotting: to show rpm vs ms the assistant rescaled the transfer-function coefficients (s -> s/1000, x1000 rpm). Its first attempt had a wrong numerator.
problems.evidence: control_response numerator '[1760.6902, 40245.124]' (wrong, x1000 too large), then '[1760.6902, 40.245124]' with t_final '600 s' standing for 600 ms.
problems.fix: plot_xy: add x_multiply / y_multiply (or x_unit/y_unit conversion), so time_s and rad/s columns can be drawn as ms and rpm without changing the model.

problems.what: Two presentation slips. The step plot puts a '50 ms target' vertical line at t = 50 ms although the spec is a 10-90 % rise time. The friction table calls 50.6 ms 'Marginal, no' although the person asked for 'about 50 ms'.
problems.evidence: plot_xy vlines '50,50 ms target'; table row '1e-4 | 50.6 ms | 0 % | Marginal, no'.
problems.fix: Mark t10 and t90 (or a band) instead of a single line at the target value.

problems.what: The assistant had Glob, Grep, Bash and Write (outside the stated tool set) and used them to find SVG paths and to write a summary HTML in its own scratchpad. The person accepted this HTML as satisfying ('both plots in an HTML page I can open') without having seen it.
problems.evidence: Turn 1 tools: Glob, Grep (on ~/.claude/projects/.../tool-results); turn 3: Bash, Write velocity_pid_summary.html.
problems.fix: In the harness, restrict tools to the brief's set, or let the simulated person open what is delivered.

what_worked: Unit trap caught at once: 'Ke = 60/(2 pi 317 rpm/V) = 0.03013 V s/rad, which matches Kt within rounding'.
Friction derived from the no-load point with electric_pm_dc_motor: 4.137 mN m and b = 5.2e-6 (truth 5.21e-6).
Pole-zero cancellation PI that matches the truth reference gains within 0.5 %, graded by truth: continuous rise 49.15 ms, 0 % overshoot, PM 89.3 deg; sampled with delay and current limit rise 51 ms.
Correct reasoning against D: the electrical pole (3624 rad/s) lies above the 1 kHz Nyquist frequency (3142 rad/s), and derivative action amplifies encoder noise.
Correct Tustin difference equation with the coefficient formula shown, and discrete closed-loop poles reported.
Useful friction sensitivity sweep, run with the tools (b up to 2e-4).
Finished in 3 turns; the person declared DONE.
